content.text: I fixed it with a one-line change in `packages/compiler-core/src/tokenizer.ts` (line 441). **Cause:** Inside `` and `<textarea>`, the tokenizer has its own code path (`stateInRCDATA`) that looks for `{{`. Unlike the normal text path, that path didn't check whether it was inside a `v-pre` block. So `{{` in a `v-pre` textarea still started an interpolation, and without a closing `}}` everything after it was swallowed. **Fix:** That `{{` check now also requires `!this.inVPre`, the same guard the normal text path already uses: ```ts } else if (!this.inVPre && c === this.delimiterOpen[0]) { ``` **Verified** with a temporary spec using the DOM compiler's `parse` (I deleted the spec afterwards) on `<div v-pre><textarea>{{ foo <div></textarea></div>`: - **Before:** parsing fails with "Interpolation end sign was not found." - **After:** the textarea holds a single text node, `{{ foo <div>`. The existing compiler-core and compiler-dom tests all pass (744). I didn't add a permanent regression test.
